    <h1>Reactor antineutrinos</h1>
  </header>

::: {.qft-exam-body}
Nuclear reactors of power plants are intense sources of antineutrinos. A reactor emits isotropically about $2\cdot 10^{20}$ antineutrinos per second for every GW of thermal power. Consider a project of experiments with reactor neutrinos.

\(i\) Compute the cross section of the interaction $\bar{\nu}_e + p \to e^+ + n$.

\(ii\) Estimate the number of such interactions per year for $E_{\bar{\nu}}=4$ MeV from a typical reactor of 3 GW. The target is water of mass 20 t. The distance between the detector and the reactor is 2 km.

\(iii\) Estimate the detector mass needed to detect $10^5$ events $\bar{\nu}_e + p \to e^+ + n$ at a distance $L=50$ km from reactors with a total power of 30 GW. Take neutrino oscillations into account.

:::
